question: 'Losar', the Ladakhi/Tibetan New Year, is welcomed with symbolic dough models representing which set of items placed in households?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ibex, Sun and Moon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Losar, the Ladakhi New Year (also the Tibetan New Year, celebrated across the Himalayan region including Arunachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Sikkim and Himachal Pradesh), is welcomed with symbolic dough models of Ibex, Sun and Moon placed in households.

 

• The Hemis Festival, another important Ladakhi celebration, features the Cham Dance, a sacred masked dance performed by monks, commemorating the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava, founder of Tibetan Buddhism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Ladakhi monastic festivals include the Matho Nagrang Festival, Tak Tok Festival and Dosmoche Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Yak/River/Mountain, Snow Leopard/Star/Cloud and Lotus/Sun/Fire (Options 2, 3, 4) are not the correct set of symbolic dough models associated with Losar, which specifically features Ibex, Sun and Moon.

question: The 'Khajuraho Dance Festival', showcasing classical dance forms like Kathak, Bharatanatyam and Odissi against the backdrop of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is held at monuments built by which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandela Dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khajuraho Dance Festival is held against the backdrop of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• These temples were built by the Chandela Dynasty.

 

• The festival showcases various Indian classical dance forms like Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Odissi and more.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh also hosts the Tansen Samaroh at Behat, Gwalior, dedicated to the legendary musician Mian Tansen, one of the Navaratnas of Emperor Akbar's court, where the National Tansen Samman is awarded annually (2025 recipient: Pandit Tarun Bhattacharya, Santoor Maestro).

 

NOTE

 

• Chola, Kakatiya and Chalukya Dynasties (Options 1, 3, 4) are associated with other monuments and festivals (such as Bastar Dussehra's origin under Kakatiya patronage, or the Pattadakal Festival's Chalukya heritage), not the Khajuraho monuments, which were built by the Chandelas.

question: The 'National Tansen Samman', awarded annually during the Tansen Samaroh at Gwalior, was awarded in 2025 to which renowned musician?
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Flute Maestro
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Tarun Bhattacharya, Santoor Maestro.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Tansen Samman, awarded annually during the Tansen Samaroh (held at Behat, Gwalior, and dedicated to the legendary musician Mian Tansen, one of the Navaratnas of Akbar's court), was awarded in 2025 to Pandit Tarun Bhattacharya, a renowned Santoor Maestro.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mian Tansen remains one of the most celebrated figures in Hindustani classical music history, credited with composing several ragas still performed today.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Zakir Hussain and Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (Options 2, 3, 4) are all legendary Indian classical musicians, but the documented 2025 recipient of the National Tansen Samman is specifically Pandit Tarun Bhattacharya.

question: 'Teej', celebrated by women in Northern and Western India to honour the reunion of Parvati and Shiva, has three main types. Which of the following correctly matches a type of Teej with its associated states?
option_1: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Hariyali Teej - Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan
option_2: Kajari Teej - Kerala and Tamil Nadu
option_4: All three types of Teej are celebrated only in Rajasthan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hariyali Teej - Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Teej is celebrated by women in Northern and Western India to honour the reunion of Parvati and Shiva, with three main types:

 

• Hariyali Teej — celebrated in Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan.

 

• Kajari Teej — celebrated in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

 

• Hartalika Teej — celebrated in Maharashtra (one day before Ganesh Chaturthi), Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan is common to all three types of Teej, reflecting the festival's especially strong cultural significance in that state.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2 and 3 incorrectly assign Kajari Teej and Hartalika Teej to states not documented in the notes, and Option 4 incorrectly restricts all Teej celebrations to Rajasthan alone.

question: 'Rann Utsav' (White Desert Festival or Kutch Festival), a massive four-month celebration of art, culture and nature, is held in the Great Rann of Kutch in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rann Utsav (White Desert Festival or Kutch Festival) is a massive four-month celebration of art, culture and nature held in the Great Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.

 

• Gujarat also hosts Navratri (celebrating the nine forms of Durga, occurring twice a year as Chaitra and Sharad Navratri) and the Vautha Fair ('Gujarat's Pushkar'), famous for its donkey market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Modhera Dance Festival and Saptak Music Festival are other notable Gujarat cultural events, alongside the Tarnetar Fair (Trinetreshwar Mahadev Festival).

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana (Options 1, 3, 4) have their own distinctive fairs and festivals, but the Rann Utsav is specifically held in Gujarat's Great Rann of Kutch.

question: 'Vautha Fair', known as 'Gujarat's Pushkar', is held at the Saptasangam in Vautha village and is famous as the only major animal trading fair in Gujarat for which specific animal market?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Donkey market.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vautha Fair, known as 'Gujarat's Pushkar', is a five-day event held at the Saptasangam in Vautha village.

 

• It is the only major animal trading fair in Gujarat and is world famous for its donkey market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat's Madhavpur Fair, another five-day festival held in Porbandar district, commemorates the marriage of Krishna and Rukmini.

 

NOTE

 

• Camel, horse and cattle markets (Options 1, 3, 4) are associated with other fairs (such as the Pushkar Camel Fair in Rajasthan or the Sonepur/Nagaur cattle fairs), not Vautha, which is specifically known for its donkey market.

question: 'Yaoshang', a five-day festival celebrated during the full moon by the Meitei community of Manipur, is often referred to by which popular alternate name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Holi of Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yaoshang, a five-day festival celebrated during the full moon by the Meitei community of Manipur, is often called the 'Holi of Manipur'.

 

• A key feature is Thabal Chongba, a folk dance where boys and girls hold hands and dance in a circle under the moonlight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Manipur festivals include Ningol Chakouba (celebrating the importance of women, where families invite married sisters/daughters for feasting and gifts) and the Sangai Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Diwali of the East, Onam of the North East and Durga Puja of Manipur (Options 2, 3, 4) are not documented alternate names for Yaoshang; its specific popular name is 'Holi of Manipur'.

question: The 'Sangai Festival' of Manipur is named after the Sangai deer, the State Animal of Manipur, found only in which unique national park?
option_2: Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park
solution_text:
The correct answer is Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangai Festival is named after the Sangai deer, the State Animal of Manipur, and promotes awareness for this endangered species.

 

• The Sangai deer is found in Keibul Lamjao National Park, located on Loktak Lake, which is described as the world's only floating national park.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Loktak Lake itself is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India and is known for its unique floating 'phumdis' (masses of vegetation, soil and organic matter), which form the basis of the floating national park.

 

NOTE

 

• Kaziranga, Manas and Nokrek National Parks (Options 1, 3, 4) are located in Assam and Meghalaya respectively, and are not associated with the Sangai deer or the Sangai Festival.

question: 'Wangala', the harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, is dedicated to which deity of fertility, also referred to as the Sun God?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Misi Saljong.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wangala, the harvest festival of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya, is dedicated to Misi Saljong, the Sun God of fertility.

 

• Shad Suk Mynsiem, a thanksgiving festival of the Khasi tribe, is offered to the Supreme Creator U Blei Trai Kynrad, and also involves worship of the Sun and Earth.

 

• Nongkrem Festival, another Khasi religious festival, is dedicated to Ka Blei Synshar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Behdienkhlam, celebrated by the Jaintia tribe, is another important Meghalaya festival, alongside Chad Laho, a folk dance festival of thanksgiving after the harvest season.

 

NOTE

 

• Ka Blei Synshar (Option 2) and U Blei Trai Kynrad (Option 3) are deities associated with Khasi festivals (Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem respectively), not Wangala. Rangkhothak (Option 4) is a deity associated with Arunachal Pradesh's Pongtu Festival of the Tutsa tribe.

question: 'Raja Parba' (Raja), a unique three-day festival of Odisha, honours womanhood and the fertility of Mother Earth by celebrating which natural biological event, believed to be undergone by Bhudevi during these days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Menstruation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Parba, a three-day Odisha festival, honours womanhood and the fertility of Mother Earth.

 

• It is unique for its celebration of menstruation; it is believed that during these days, Bhudevi (Mother Earth) undergoes her menstrual cycle and prepares for the upcoming agricultural season.

 

• The festival is observed by young girls with swings and songs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This theme closely parallels Assam's Ambubachi Mela, which similarly celebrates the annual menstruation of Goddess Kamakhya as a symbol of Mother Earth's fertility.

 

NOTE

 

• Childbirth, marriage and pregnancy (Options 1, 3, 4) do not correctly describe the specific biological event (menstruation) celebrated during Raja Parba.

question: 'Dhanu Jatra' (Dhanu Yatra), an 11-day festival held in Bargarh, Odisha, has been recognised by the Guinness World Records for which distinction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is World's largest open-air theatre.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhanu Jatra (Dhanu Yatra), a massive 11-day festival held in Bargarh, Odisha, is recognised as the world's largest open-air theatre by the Guinness World Records.

 

• The festival dramatically enacts episodes from the life of Lord Krishna, using the entire town of Bargarh and surrounding areas as its stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bali Yatra, another important Odisha festival, is celebrated in Cuttack on the banks of the Mahanadi, commemorating ancient maritime trade links with Southeast Asia (Bali).

 

NOTE

 

• 'World's largest floating festival', 'longest chariot procession' and 'largest tribal congregation' (Options 1, 3, 4) are distinctions associated with other events (such as Medaram Jatara for tribal congregation), not Dhanu Jatra, whose specific Guinness recognition is for the world's largest open-air theatre.

question: 'Atla Taddi', a festival of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh in which married women fast for their husbands' longevity, is considered the South Indian equivalent of which North Indian festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karva Chauth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Atla Taddi, occurring on the third night after the full moon in the Telugu month of Aswayuja, is considered equivalent to Karva Chauth of North India.

 

• Married women observe a fast to pray for the longevity and well-being of their husbands, while unmarried girls perform rituals to pray for a suitable and loving life partner.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Andhra Pradesh/Telangana festivals include Kanuma (honouring cattle used in agriculture, celebrated on the third day of the four-day Makar Sankranti festival) and Rotela Panduga (marked by the offering and sharing of rotis).

 

NOTE

 

• Rakhi, Bhai Dooj and Vat Savitri (Options 1, 3, 4) are other significant North Indian festivals, but none carries the specific 'fasting for husband's longevity' parallel that Atla Taddi shares with Karva Chauth.

question: 'Ugadi' (Yugadi), the Hindu New Year believed to mark the day Brahma began the creation of the universe, is celebrated under the same name in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, but by which name in Karnataka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yugadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ugadi (Yugadi), believed to mark the day Brahma began the creation of the universe, is celebrated as Ugadi in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and as Yugadi in Karnataka.

 

• In Maharashtra and Goa, the same day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa.

 

• The day traditionally begins with an Oil Bath (Abhyanjana Snanam) — a ceremonial bath after a sesame oil massage, believed to purify the body and spirit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This is another example (alongside Baisakhi's regional names) of a single astronomical New Year being celebrated under different regional names across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Vishu (Option 1) is Kerala's New Year, and Puthandu (Option 4) is Tamil Nadu's New Year, both linked to the Baisakhi solar transition rather than the Chaitra-based Ugadi/Yugadi/Gudi Padwa group. Gudi Padwa (Option 3) is Maharashtra/Goa's name for the same day, not Karnataka's.

question: 'Hola Mohalla', a Punjab festival celebrating the birth of Guru Gobind Singh, showcases martial arts, langars and mock battles at which historic site?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anandpur Sahib.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hola Mohalla showcases martial arts, langars, and Nihang mock battles at Anandpur Sahib, celebrating the birth of Guru Gobind Singh.

 

• Other Punjab festivals include Lohri (marking the end of winter solstice) and Gurpurab (commemorating the birth or life events of the ten Sikh Gurus, observed multiple times a year).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hola Mohalla is traditionally celebrated a day after Holi, and the Nihang Sikhs' displays of horse-riding and swordsmanship are a central highlight of the event.

 

NOTE

 

• Golden Temple (Amritsar), Fatehgarh Sahib and Talwandi Sabo (Options 1, 3, 4) are other significant Sikh historical sites, but Hola Mohalla's martial displays are specifically centred at Anandpur Sahib.

question: 'Surajkund Crafts Mela', held in Haryana, is known by which distinction, showcasing traditional Indian handicrafts, handlooms, folk dances and cultural performances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is World's largest crafts fair.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Surajkund Crafts Mela, held in Haryana, is known as the world's largest crafts fair, showcasing traditional Indian handicrafts, handlooms, folk dances and cultural performances.

 

• Other Haryana events include the Pinjore Heritage Festival (at the historic Pinjore Gardens) and the International Gita Mahotsav (Kurukshetra Festival), which commemorates the birth of the Bhagavad Gita at Kurukshetra, where Krishna is believed to have delivered its teachings to Arjuna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Haryana also observes Gugga Naumi, a snake-worship festival dedicated to Gugga Peer, celebrated across Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Asia's largest', 'India's oldest' and 'world's smallest' (Options 1, 3, 4) do not correctly describe Surajkund Crafts Mela's documented distinction, which is specifically 'world's largest crafts fair'.

question: 'International Gita Mahotsav' (Kurukshetra Festival), celebrated in Kurukshetra, commemorates the birth of the Bhagavad Gita, where Lord Krishna is believed to have delivered its teachings to whom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arjuna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Gita Mahotsav (Kurukshetra Festival) is celebrated in Kurukshetra, commemorating the birth of the Bhagavad Gita, where Krishna is believed to have delivered its teachings to Arjuna on the battlefield before the start of the Mahabharata war.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kurukshetra, in Haryana, is revered as a major site of Mahabharata-related heritage and hosts several cultural and religious events tied to this epic.

 

NOTE

 

• Yudhishthira, Bhishma and Duryodhana (Options 1, 3, 4) are other significant figures in the Mahabharata, but the Bhagavad Gita's teachings were specifically delivered to Arjuna.

question: 'Thrissur Pooram', considered Kerala's most spectacular temple festival, is distinct from 'Kollam Pooram'. What is the correct relationship between these two, as per the notes?
option_1: Thrissur Pooram is Kerala's most famous Pooram, while Kollam Pooram is the largest Pooram in southern Kerala
option_2: Kollam Pooram is more famous than Thrissur Pooram overall
option_3: Both festivals are identical and celebrated on the same day at the same temple
option_4: Thrissur Pooram is dedicated to Krishna, and Kollam Pooram is dedicated to Ayyappa
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thrissur Pooram is Kerala's most famous Pooram, while Kollam Pooram is the largest Pooram in southern Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thrissur Pooram is considered Kerala's most spectacular temple festival, and is the most famous Pooram overall.

 

• Kollam Pooram, celebrated in Kollam and dedicated to Krishna, is specifically the largest Pooram in southern Kerala, distinct from (though related in tradition to) Thrissur Pooram.

 

• 'Pooram' means a 'group' or 'meeting', historically referring to the gathering of gods and goddesses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Kerala celebrations include the Attukal Pongala and the Nishagandhi Festival, a cultural arts festival held in Thiruvananthapuram.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 incorrectly reverses their relative fame; Option 3 incorrectly claims they are identical; Option 4 incorrectly reverses the deity association — Kollam Pooram, not Thrissur Pooram, is linked to Krishna as per the notes.

question: Which of the following tribal festivals of Jharkhand is correctly matched with its significance?
option_1: Sarhul - means 'worship of the Sal tree'
option_2: Tusu Festival - a cattle and harvest festival celebrated by the Ho Tribe
option_4: Mage Parab - primarily a festival of the Santhal Tribe in West Bengal only
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarhul - means 'worship of the Sal tree'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sarhul means 'worship of the Sal tree', marking the tribal new year in Jharkhand.

 

• Tusu Festival (Tusu Parab) is celebrated by the Santhal Tribe, primarily in the tribal belt of Jharkhand around Bundu, Tamar and Raidih — not specifically a 'cattle and harvest festival of the Ho Tribe' (that description applies more closely to the general Sohrai Festival).

 

• Baha Parab (Ba Parab) means the 'Flower Festival' ('Ba' means flower), celebrated by the Santhal, Ho and Munda tribes, not a snake-worship festival.

 

• Mage Parab is a festival of the Ho Tribe in Jharkhand AND West Bengal, not exclusively West Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jawa Festival, part of the Karma Festival, involves germinated seeds symbolising new life and fertility, especially significant for young women.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 each contain a factual error regarding the specific tribe, theme, or geographic scope of the named festival, as detailed in the important points above.

question: 'Sohrai Festival', a cattle and harvest festival celebrated in Jharkhand and Bihar, is observed to express gratitude to nature and livestock, and typically follows which major festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diwali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sohrai Festival, a cattle and harvest festival of Jharkhand and Bihar, is celebrated to express gratitude to nature and livestock for their role in the agricultural cycle, and is celebrated immediately after Diwali.

 

• This mirrors similar cattle-thanksgiving traditions like Maharashtra/Chhattisgarh's Pola Festival and Andhra Pradesh/Telangana's Kanuma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bandna Festival, celebrated across Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Assam, is similarly associated with domestic animals (cows and bulls) essential to agriculture.

 

NOTE

 

• Holi, Dussehra and Makar Sankranti (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the festival after which Sohrai is specifically timed; that is Diwali.

question: 'Pola Festival', a thanksgiving festival dedicated to bulls and oxen honouring their role in agriculture, is primarily celebrated in which two states, though also observed in parts of Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pola Festival is primarily celebrated in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, though its observance also extends to parts of Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

 

• This thanksgiving festival is dedicated to bulls and oxen, honouring their indispensable role in agriculture and farming.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhattisgarh's Hareli Festival, occurring on the new moon day of Shravan, similarly involves farmers worshipping agricultural equipment, bullocks and cows — a related agrarian tradition observed in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand as 'Harela'.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab/Haryana, Bihar/Jharkhand and Kerala/Tamil Nadu (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the primary states associated with Pola Festival, which is specifically centred on Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

question:
Consider the following statements about the 'Karma Festival':
1. It is a tribal harvest festival dedicated to Karam Devta, revolving around the Karam tree on Bhadra Ekadashi.
2. It is celebrated only in Jharkhand and nowhere else.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The Karma Festival is a tribal harvest festival dedicated to Karam Devta, and revolves around the Karam tree on Bhadra Ekadashi, worshipped as a symbol of fertility and prosperity.

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: Karma Festival is celebrated across Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and West Bengal — not exclusively in Jharkhand.

 

• Karma Nach is the associated dance performed during this festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This multi-state spread of the Karma Festival parallels the similarly widespread Jhumar folk dance, both reflecting shared tribal-agrarian traditions across central and eastern India.

 

NOTE

 

• Since Statement 2 incorrectly restricts Karma Festival's celebration to Jharkhand alone, any option marking it correct is wrong.

question: 'Cherchera Festival', celebrated in Chhattisgarh on the full moon day of the Hindu month of Paush, marks the end of which agricultural activity and is described as a celebration of the 'spirit of giving'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paddy harvest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cherchera Festival, celebrated in Chhattisgarh on the full moon day of the Hindu month Paush, is a celebration of agricultural abundance and the 'spirit of giving', marking the end of the paddy harvest.

 

• This is distinct from Hareli Festival, which occurs earlier in the agricultural calendar on the new moon day of Shravan, when farmers worship their agricultural equipment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhattisgarh's rich festival calendar also includes Madai Festival (a moving festival observed by the Gond Tribe from village to village between December and March).

 

NOTE

 

• Wheat sowing, cotton picking and sugarcane cutting (Options 1, 3, 4) are not the agricultural activity marked by Cherchera; that is specifically the paddy harvest.

question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 'Feast of Saint Francis Xavier' and 'São João Festival', both celebrated in Goa?
option_1: The Feast of Saint Francis Xavier commemorates his death anniversary; São João Festival is dedicated to John the Baptist
option_2: Both festivals commemorate the same saint on the same day
option_3: The Feast of Saint Francis Xavier is dedicated to John the Baptist; São João Festival commemorates Francis Xavier's death
option_4: Neither festival has any Christian religious association
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Feast of Saint Francis Xavier commemorates his death anniversary; São João Festival is dedicated to John the Baptist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Feast of Saint Francis Xavier commemorates the death anniversary of Francis Xavier, a founding member of the Society of Jesus and a pioneer missionary in Asia.

 

• São João Festival is dedicated to John the Baptist, reflecting Goa's strong Portuguese Catholic heritage.

 

• Goa's diverse festival calendar also includes Shigmo (Goa's version of Holi) and the Sunburn Festival (also celebrated in Gujarat and Maharashtra).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Goa's unique blend of Indian and Portuguese cultural influences is also reflected in the folk dance Dekhni and the historic Bonderam Festival (Festival of Flags).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 incorrectly conflate, reverse, or deny the distinct Christian religious associations of these two separate Goan festivals.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Dol Jatra' festival:
1. It is observed in Assam, Odisha and West Bengal.
2. It is dedicated to the divine love of Radha and Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Dol Jatra is observed in Assam, Odisha and West Bengal.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: It is dedicated to the divine love of Radha and Krishna, aligning it thematically with other Krishna-Radha festivals like Uttar Pradesh's Raslila.

 

• Dol Jatra typically coincides with the Holi season and involves the ceremonial swinging of deity idols.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Assam's broader festival calendar also includes the Assam Tea Festival (celebrated in Jorhat, the 'Tea Capital of the World') and Baisagu, marking the Bodo New Year.

 

NOTE

 

• Since both statements are verified as correct from the notes, options selecting only one statement are incorrect.

question: Which of the following is the correct set of festival-state pairings, all verified as per the state-wise festivals and fairs survey?
option_1: Hornbill Festival - Nagaland; Onam - Kerala; Bathukamma - Telangana; Bastar Dussehra - Chhattisgarh
option_2: Hornbill Festival - Manipur; Onam - Tamil Nadu; Bathukamma - Karnataka; Bastar Dussehra - Odisha
option_3: Hornbill Festival - Mizoram; Onam - Andhra Pradesh; Bathukamma - Gujarat; Bastar Dussehra - Maharashtra
option_4: Hornbill Festival - Tripura; Onam - Karnataka; Bathukamma - Punjab; Bastar Dussehra - Rajasthan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hornbill Festival - Nagaland; Onam - Kerala; Bathukamma - Telangana; Bastar Dussehra - Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hornbill Festival is celebrated at Kisama Heritage Village in Nagaland.

 

• Onam, the harvest festival marking Mahabali's homecoming, is celebrated in Kerala.

 

• Bathukamma, the floral festival honouring Goddess Gauri, is celebrated in Telangana.

 

• Bastar Dussehra, the world's longest festival dedicated to Danteshwari, is celebrated in Chhattisgarh.

 

• Correctly memorising such festival-state pairings, alongside dance-state and language-state pairings, is one of the highest-yield preparation strategies for the Static GK section of SSC examinations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cross-verifying such pairings against multiple static-GK categories (dance, music, festivals, temples) helps build a consistent, error-free knowledge base for the exam.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 incorrectly reassign these festivals to states with no documented association in the notes for these specific events.
